translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui stationed five thousand men under him at Longling Pass for deployment.

sentences.zh: 召詣熱河行在，入見，命乾清門行走，賜貂皮、銀幣，令還軍。

translations.literal: Summoned to the imperial residence at Rehe for audience, he was ordered to serve at the Gate of Celestial Purity, granted sable fur and silver coin, and ordered back to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the emperor at Rehe, he was ordered to serve at the Gate of Celestial Purity, granted sable fur and silver, and sent back to the army.

sentences.zh: 旋移普洱鎮總兵，擢雲南提督。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to regional commander of the Pu'er garrison and promoted to provincial commander of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Pu'er as regional commander and promoted to provincial commander of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 卒，加太子太保，諡勤毅。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous epithet Qinyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously raised to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Qinyi.

sentences.zh: 劉順，順天人。

translations.literal: Liu Shun was a native of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shun was from the capital district.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年武進士，授藍翎侍衛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng he passed the military metropolitan examination and was appointed Blue-Lapel Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the military metropolitan examination in 1727 and was made a Blue-Lapel Bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 以守備發陝西。

translations.literal: He was dispatched to Shaanxi as a garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Shaanxi as a garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 累遷至金塔協副將。

translations.literal: He was promoted successively to brigade deputy of the Jinta garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to deputy commander at Jinta.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年，令將千五百人赴金川，偕副將高雄自甲索攻囊得，道松林。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong he was ordered to lead fifteen hundred men to Jinchuan; together with Brigade Deputy Commander Gao Xiong he attacked Nangde from Jiasuo by way of the pine forest.
translations.idiomatic: In 1748 he led fifteen hundred men to Jinchuan and, with Deputy Commander Gao Xiong, attacked Nangde from Jiasuo through the pine woods.

sentences.zh: 賊百餘出戰，擊之遁，毀賊碉。

translations.literal: More than a hundred rebels came out to fight; he struck them and they fled, destroying rebel blockhouses.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred rebels sallied; he drove them off and destroyed their blockhouses.

sentences.zh: 從大軍自卡撒左山梁進，諸碉以次皆下。

translations.literal: Following the main army from the left ridge of Kasa, the blockhouses fell one after another.
translations.idiomatic: With the main army from Kasa's left ridge, the blockhouses fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 惟普瞻雙、單二碉守甚堅。

translations.literal: Only the twin and single blockhouses at Puzhan held extremely firm.
translations.idiomatic: Only the twin and single blockhouses at Puzhan held out stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 日暮，將收兵，順潛率所部逼單碉，縱火攻之，賊潰，並奪雙碉。

translations.literal: At dusk, as the army was about to withdraw, Shun secretly led his unit to press the single blockhouse, set fire to attack it, the rebels scattered, and he also seized the twin blockhouses.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk, as troops were pulling back, Shun secretly led his men against the single blockhouse, set it afire, routed the defenders, and took the twin blockhouses as well.

sentences.zh: 師繼進，遂克色底。

translations.literal: The army pressed forward and then captured Sedi.
translations.idiomatic: The main force pressed on and took Sedi.

sentences.zh: 普瞻西有山曰阿利，賊碉林立。

translations.literal: West of Puzhan was a mountain called Ali where rebel blockhouses stood in dense array.
translations.idiomatic: West of Puzhan stood Mount Ali, thick with rebel blockhouses.

sentences.zh: 順冒雨奮攻，奪山樑木卡，破碉。

translations.literal: Shun attacked fiercely in the rain, seized the ridge wooden barrier, and broke blockhouses.
translations.idiomatic: Shun attacked through the rain, took the ridge barrier, and broke the blockhouses.

sentences.zh: 發砲，殪賊數十，复破大碉一、石卡四。

translations.literal: He fired cannon, killed several dozen rebels, and again broke one great blockhouse and four stone barriers.
translations.idiomatic: With cannon he killed dozens of rebels and took one great blockhouse and four stone barriers.

sentences.zh: 經略訥親屢奏順奮勇。

translations.literal: Commissioner Neqin repeatedly memorialized Shun's valor.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Neqin repeatedly reported Shun's valor.

sentences.zh: 金川平，擢貴州威寧鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When Jinchuan was pacified he was promoted to regional commander of the Weining garrison in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinchuan was pacified he was made regional commander at Weining in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 上以順熟邊情，移甘肅西寧鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Because the emperor said Shun knew border conditions well, he was transferred to regional commander of the Xining garrison in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him expert in frontier affairs and transferred him to regional commander at Xining in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 入見，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: On audience he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: At court he was granted the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 擢安西提督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial commander of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial commander of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 病，乞罷。

translations.literal: Ill, he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Falling ill, he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 卒，加太子太保，諡壯靖。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous epithet Zhuangjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously raised to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Zhuangjing.

sentences.zh: 論曰：初徵金川，攀龍、舉、大雄皆以勇略著。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the first Jinchuan campaign, Panlong, Ju, and Daxiong were all noted for courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In the first Jinchuan campaign, Panlong, Ju, and Daxiong were all famed for courage and strategy.

sentences.zh: 舉尤驍桀為軍鋒，訥親、張廣泗督戰急，鼓銳攻堅，遂以身殉，傷已！

translations.literal: Ju was especially fierce and served as the army's spearhead; Neqin and Zhang Guangsi pressed the fighting urgently, rousing elite troops to assault strong positions, and thus he gave his life—a grievous loss!
translations.idiomatic: Ju was the fiercest vanguard of the army; Neqin and Zhang Guangsi drove the fighting hard, hurling crack troops against strongholds until Ju fell—a grievous loss!

sentences.zh: 良柱善戰，又以廣泗牽制，不能盡其材。

translations.literal: Liangzhu was skilled in battle, yet because Guangsi held him back he could not fully display his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhu was a skilled fighter, but Guangsi's interference kept him from showing his full ability.

sentences.zh: 進忠、順力戰破堅碉，亦攀龍輩之亞也。

translations.literal: Jinzhong and Shun fought hard to break strong blockhouses and ranked next to men like Panlong.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong and Shun fought hard to break stubborn blockhouses and stood only a step below men like Panlong.
